sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to enmity and village rivalry.
The entire allegations are levelled against the appellant with intention to defame his image as well as his entire family in the society.
No such incident as alleged by the prosecution took place.

As per the version of the F.I.R., when the prosecutrix was alone in her house, the appellant alongwith two other persons, namely, Veer Pal and Madhuraj Singh came in her house and the co-accused Veer Pal committed rape upon the prosecutrix whereas the appellant and co-accused Madhuraj Singh were having country made tamancha and they were threatening the prosecutrix.
It is further stated in the F.I.R. that when all the accused were leaving her house, the appellant threatened her with dire consequences.
It is also stated in the F.I.R. that husband of the prosecutrix was not present at the alleged time of incident.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has almost reiterated the version of F.I.R. and has made specific allegation against the Veer Pal about commission of rape upon her whereas against the appellant and co-accused Madhuraj Singh, she has stated that they were standing near the door of the room and were having country made tamancha.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has levelled allegation of rape only against Veer Pal about commission of rape and for the appellant as well as Madhuraj Singh, she slightly modified her statement by stating that they were only standing near the door of the room, however, no allegation of possession of country made tamancha is assigned to the co-accused Shishu Pal and the appellant.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the husband of the prosecutrix was having enmity with Veer Pal and the appellant being brother of the main accused, Veer Pal, has been implicated in the present case.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that medical report of the prosecutrix does not corroborate with the allegation of commission of rape as the doctor has clearly opined that no mark of injury was present on any part of the body except 0.5 cm below an old scar was present on left arm medial aspect 6.5 cm from nostrial.

He further submits that the doctor also opined that no mark of injury was found on the private part of the body of the prosecutrix, the age of the prosecutrix is about 45 years and finally the doctor opined that no definite opinion could be given regarding sexual assault.
Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the case of the present appellant is totally distinguishable from Veer Pal, who is the main accused.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that similarly circumstanced and identically placed co-accused, Madhuraj Singh has already been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 14.07.2023 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 2481 of 2022 and the case of the appellant is not on the worse footing than that of the co-accused, who has been granted bail, therefore, the appellant may also be enlarged on bail by this Court on the ground of parity.

sentences.text: Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the appellant have also been placed forth before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused have also been touched upon at length.

It has been assured on behalf of the appellant that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required and is also ready to accept all the conditions which the Court may deem fit to impose upon him.

It has also been pointed out that the accused is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 31.10.2021 and that in the wake of heavy pendency of cases in the Court, there is no likelihood of any early conclusion of trial.

Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 as well as learned A.G.A. for the State have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that this is a case of gang rape and the role of all the accused are similar, however, they are unable to dispute the fact that the allegation of commission of rape has been levelled against the main accused i.e. Veer Pal and the appellant has only been assigned role of standing near the door of the room and no allegation of commission of rape has been levelled against him.
They have also not disputed the fact that medical report does not corroborate with the prosecution story as no injury was found on the private part of the body of the prosecutrix.

After perusing the record in the light of the submissions made at the bar and after taking an overall view of all the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence, the period of detention already undergone, the unlikelihood of early conclusion of trial and also in the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence and considering the fact that as per the version of the F.I.R. as well as the statements of the prosecution recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the allegation of rape has been levelled against the main accused Veer Pal whereas no allegation of rape has been levelled against the present appellant.

As per the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the allegation of possession of country made pistol is levelled against the appellant whereas she has changed her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., and has only stated that the appellant was only standing near the door of the room.

The medical report also does not corroborate with the allegation of rape as the doctor has opined that no mark of internal or external injury was found on the person of the prosecutrix, her age was found to be of 45 years and even there was no eye witness of the alleged incident and her husband was also not present in the house at the time of incident.

Further considering that similarly circumstanced and identically placed co-accused, Madhuraj Singh has already been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 14.07.2023 passed in Criminal Appeal No.
2481 of 2022 and further considering the larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Dataram Singh vs. State of UP and another, reported in (2018) 3 SCC 22, this Court is of the view that the learned court below has failed to appreciate the material available on record.

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the appellant, Shishupal Yadav be released on bail in the Case Crime No.167 of 2015, under Sections 376-D, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)V of S.C./S.T. Act, Police Station Aaseewan, District Unnao with the following conditions:-
(i) The appellant shall furnish a personal bond with two sureties each of like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.

(ii) The appellant shall appear and strictly comply following terms of bond executed under section 437 sub section 3 of Chapter- 33 of Cr.P.C.:-
(a) The appellant shall attend in accordance with the conditions of the bond executed under this Chapter.
(b) The appellant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected, and (c) The appellant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The appellant shall cooperate with investigation /trial.
(iv) The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(v) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(vi) In case, the appellant misuses the liberty of bail during trial, in order to secure his presence, proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the appellant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(vii) The appellant shall remain present, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and Shishupal Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82660705/
